cards.explanation: The answer is to praise the name of the LORD. The writer says, "Give praise, O servants of the LORD; praise the name of the LORD." He says it right after "Hallelujah!" so he's clearly warmed up. I think a psalm that starts this loud is hard to ignore, friends.

The answer is False. The writer says, "Blessed be the name of the LORD both now and forevermore." Feast days never come up in the verse. Both now and forevermore covers a LOT more days than a feast calendar does, friends.
The answer is above the heavens. The writer says, "The LORD is exalted over all the nations, His glory above the heavens." Over all the nations AND above the heavens. That's a big reach, friends.

The answer is that no one is like Him. The writer asks, "Who is like the LORD our God, the One enthroned on high?" I think he's asking it to make you say it out loud: nobody. He doesn't hand over a list of names. He lets the question hang there, friends.

The answer is True. The psalm says, "He humbles Himself to behold the heavens and the earth." Think about that, friends. The One enthroned on high stoops to look at the heavens AND the earth. That's the God of this psalm.
The answer is poor. The psalm says, "He raises the poor from the dust…" The One enthroned on high reaches down for the poor. I think that's one of the best lines in the whole psalm, friends.

The answer is with the princes of His people. The psalm says He lifts the needy "…to seat them with nobles, with the princes of His people." They go from the dump to a seat with princes. That's a promotion no résumé could get you, friends.

The answer is barren. The psalm says, "He settles the barren woman in her home as a joyful mother to her children." It doesn't tell us how it happens. It just gives us the picture of a joyful mother at home. Then comes the final "Hallelujah!"
